about: The blind classification of revision 1's claim reasons (the `why` the claim judge gave each claim) from the claim judge round's three revision 1 passes (results/judge-v5/stage-a-rev1.json, .judge-s2.json and .judge-s3.json). Two readers classified reasons blind to the answer key, the label and the score: the first reader all three batches below, the second reader every claim scored 50 to 85 in a judging whose weakest claim is 50 or more, which holds batch 1; only its batch 1 classes are joined here. Each reader's key map was written by a seeded shuffle and read only after the classes were saved; both maps are recomputed from the pass files here and found equal. Every answer_span, role, score, quoted flag and why below is copied from the pass files; the readers' files hold only their classes. No committed script writes this file: it was assembled once from the readers' class files, which are kept outside the repository, and the pass files. Nothing was judged anew, and no call was made. The classes describe the judge's stated reasons on saved passes; they decide nothing.

classes.RW: plain rewording, arithmetic or a unit conversion of what a quote states
classes.EXT: an implication or extension beyond the quote
classes.NAME: a name or term in no quote
classes.QUAL: a qualifier or scope beyond the quote
classes.OTHER: another gap, with its kind: a headerless table cell, or a claim that depends on the current date

class_rule.reader_1: Blind classification of revision 1's weakest-claim why texts (scores 50 to 85), made before the key map or labels were read. ST stated outright; RW plain rewording or arithmetic; EXT mild extension or implication; NAME a name or term in no quote; QUAL a qualifier or scope beyond the quote; OTHER (hdr: a table cell read without its header; date: depends on the current date). amb: the why's own wording straddles two classes, alt is the other reading. Rule: a why that names no gap is ST (the quote states it) or RW (it follows); a why that names a gap takes the class of the gap it names first.
class_rule.reader_1_batch_2: Blind classes for batch 2: claims scored 70 to 85 that are not the weakest, in answers revision 1 passes at t = 70. Same classes and rule as batch 1.
class_rule.reader_1_batch_3: Blind classes for batch 3: claims scored above 85 in answers revision 1 passes at t = 70 whose why passed a broad reservation-word screen (the 204 screened out all read as stated or reworded). Same classes and rule.
class_rule.reader_2:
Class rule, fixed before reading any why text (2026-10-29). Read the why only. A why that names
no gap is ST or RW; a why that names a gap takes the class of the FIRST gap it names.

ST    the quote states it (directly, explicitly, verbatim, "quote N says", "the row/header shows"),
      and no gap is named.
RW    it follows by rewording, paraphrase, summary, arithmetic or a unit conversion, or "follows
      from" a stated fact, and no gap is named.
EXT   an inference, implication or extension beyond the quote ("implies", "reasonable inference",
      "mild extension", "suggests", "inferred"), with no specific missing term and no qualifier
      named as the gap.
NAME  a specific name, term, feature, product, version, edition, API, error, unit or value that no
      quote contains or names ("no quote mentions X", "doesn't name X", "X is not stated").
QUAL  a qualifier or scope beyond the quote: only/sole/always/all/by default/never, a scope or
      condition the quote does not tie the fact to ("not explicitly about X", "not clearly the
      sole starting point", "subject to change not shown").
Other a table cell or row quoted without its header; a fact that needs the current date; any
      other gap not above.

Ambiguous items carry an alternative class (written as CLASS|ALT).

batches.1: the weakest claims scored 50 to 85 over revision 1's three passes (every claim tied at the lowest score of its judging); read by both readers
batches.2: claims scored 70 to 85 that are not the weakest, in answers revision 1 passes at t = 70 with s off; read by the first reader
batches.3: claims scored above 85 in answers revision 1 passes at t = 70 with s off whose reason passed a reservation-word screen (204 such claims were screened out and read as stated or reworded); read by the first reader
